title: MAX ( -2, BLANK() ) with two scalar arguments is BLANK

source.quote: MAX consider the BLANK value as significative, whereas MAXX ignores it
source.supports: the page gives the two-argument form as a SWITCH and says MAX ( -2, BLANK() ) returns BLANK

source.quote: blank is treated as 0 when comparing
source.supports: the other reading: Max( -1, Blank() ) returns 0

derivation: DAX Guide's expansion: v1 = -2, v2 = BLANK. v1 = v2 is FALSE (-2 is not 0). v1 > v2 is FALSE (-2 is not greater than BLANK, which compares as 0). So the result is v2, which is BLANK.
alternative: The Microsoft page says Max( -1, Blank() ) returns 0: BLANK is not only compared as 0 but returned as 0. Under that reading the result is the integer 0, not BLANK.
notes: The two readings differ only in ISBLANK of the result: BLANK and 0 are equal under =. The column's type is not asserted.
